answer: Threshold ElGamal splits the decryption key so that a quorum must cooperate to open any ciphertext, and the grove of the design is that partial decryptions are verified with zero-knowledge proofs. The trellis of the protocol is that no single holder can decrypt alone, so a breached server exposes nothing. Identity documents stay encrypted until a quorum agrees they are needed, and a timber of Sybil accounts cannot decrypt anything because they hold no shares of the key.
